messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: multi-GPU collective stalls detected on cluster prod-gpu-cluster-8. Severity: potential P1. Observed repeated NCCL_TUNNEL_TIMEOUT and CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS on several TensorParallel jobs. Pager triggered to eng-runtime.
jamie: saw this at ~09:11 UTC, first noticed npipeline-04 job stuck in allreduce. Pod restarted twice then OOMKilled. Logs excerpt: 
```
[2026-02-28T09:11:24Z] NCCL WARN Call to ncclCommInitAll returned NCCL_INTERNAL_ERROR
[2026-02-28T09:11:25Z] cuda: 0: Xid 79: GPU page fault, likely context corrupted, resetting GPU
[2026-02-28T09:11:25Z] pid 24312: container restart (OOM?)
```
jamie: kubectl describe pod shows terminationReason=OOMKilled and node dmesg shows repeated GPU resets. Suspect interaction between quantized kernels and driver 525.x under large TP batch sizes.
liam: I'm paged, taking incident. Quick checklist: 1) confirm customer impact 2) apply routing fallback 3) cordon/drain problematic nodes 4) coordinate driver/AMI rollback if needed.
maria-product: customer triage: AcmeAI and FinLabs reported increased tail latency and a few failed inference jobs. CS counted ~12 failed jobs in last 30m across those two tenants. Currently affecting streaming and batch inference routes with TensorParallel enabled.
liam: immediate mitigations proposed: 
- route impacted customers to single-GPU model-variant (runtime fallback)
- set REDWOOD_RUNTIME_FALLBACK=1 for affected routes
- cordon/evacuate nodes showing repeated Xid resets
- reduce TP batch-size and disable aggressive KV caching
Please ack if able to run these.
kavya: I can take handoff in ~10m. I'll run evacuation script and start node-level remediation: `./scripts/drain-gpu-node --selector=node=prod-gpu-8 --grace-period=30`. Note: draining will kill in-flight TP contexts. Prefer routing fallback first to avoid user-visible failures.
chipops: agreed. applying fallback now to acme-ai route: `redwood route update acme-ai --model rwd/sm-1gpu-fallback --env REDWOOD_RUNTIME_FALLBACK=1`
jamie: fallback applied. Warmup observed successful on 2 instances; error rate for that customer dropped to baseline.
liam: checking infra: `nvidia-smi -q -d PIDS,FB_USAGE` shows repeated FB resets and multiple processes with stale device contexts. NCCL debug logs show `ncclCommAbort()` from rank 2 during allreduce.
liam: creating SEV ticket and escalating to ENG_RUNTIME + ENG_INFRA. Owners: jamie (runtime) and kavya (ops).
incident-bot: PagerDuty: escalated to eng-runtime. Oncall liam handing off to kavya at 09:27 UTC.
kavya: taking over. Action plan: 1) apply temporary kernel workarounds to disable quantized kernel path, 2) roll driver back to 525.80 on suspect nodes, 3) if rollback unavailable, cordon and reprovision nodes with known-good AMI, 4) keep runtime fallback until all nodes healthy. Starting rollout on node group prod-gpu-group-3.
chipops: preparing hotfix: restart kubelet and clear NCCL stale resources: `ssh node && sudo systemctl restart kubelet && sudo /opt/nccl/cleanup.sh`. Also will sequence reboots to avoid mass eviction.
jamie: enabling KV cache disable for affected routes to reduce memory pressure: set REDWOOD_KV_CACHE=false. This should lower peak FB usage and reduce chance of page faults.
kavya: cordoned gpu-8 and started draining; 3/5 nodes in group rebooting. One node failed to come up due to missing driver module after reboot -> infra bug created. Rolling continue with lock-step.
liam: handover note for postmortem: initial root cause hypothesis - interplay between quantized kernels (recent opt) and driver 525.x under large TP batch sizes leading to GPU page faults (Xid 79) and subsequent NCCL communicator aborts. Mitigations that worked: runtime fallback to single-GPU model, KV cache disable, coordinated node drain/rollback.
maria-product: customer communication: messages sent to AcmeAI and FinLabs at 09:40 UTC explaining transient failures and mitigation steps. CS opened credit requests for impacted customers; recommend legal/finance review for credits.
jamie: post-incident action items (PIA): 
- add detector that alerts on repeated GPU Xid resets per node (threshold: 3 in 5m)
- add runbook step to prefer routing fallback before draining TP nodes
- add driver compatibility matrix tests including quantized kernels + TP stress harness
- review recent quantized kernel changes and revert if necessary
kavya: I'll own the postmortem doc and coordinate with eng-runtime and infra. Tagging @eng-runtime @infra for follow-ups.
liam: final impact summary: no customer data exposure; service-level degradation approximated at ~7% of GPU cluster capacity for ~40 minutes; stable state restored by ~09:50 UTC after fallbacks and node rollbacks.
incident-bot: Incident marked resolved by kavya at 09:55 UTC. Runbook reference: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/nccl-collective-stalls.
